{{Quote|Their world is sprinkled with thousands of rock pillars. Most of the best food plants grow on the tops. Unfortunately, so does a nasty predator avian.|Dubrak Qennto|<ref name="OF" />}}
'''Pashvi''' was a [[Planet/Legends|planet]] that was located on the edge of [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]] and had thousands of rock pillars scattered across its landscape. Both [[Diet/Legends|nutritional]] [[Unidentified plant (Pashvi)|plants]] and dangerous [[Unidentified Pashvi avian|predatory avians]] could be found on the tops of the pillars. As a result, the native [[Pashvi (species)|Pashvi]], a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] [[Species/Legends|species]], were both drawn to and afraid of the pillars, and had a distanced emotional state. The Pashvi also created works of art that were sought after in the [[Corporate Sector/Legends|Corporate Sector]], and the [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Dubrak Qennto]] had visited the world a few [[Time/Legends|times]] by the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[27 BBY/Legends|27 BBY]].

==Description==
Pashvi was a remote [[Planet/Legends|planet]] with at least one [[Star/Legends|sun]]<ref name="CSWE" /> that was located within the [[Pashvi system/Legends|Pashvi system]],<ref name="EAOC" /><ref name="Planetnamia" /> on the edge of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy's]] [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]] region. Thousands of rock pillars were scattered across the planet's surface,<ref name="OF" /> and certain [[Unidentified plant (Pashvi)|plants]] grew on the tops of those pillars, where they could receive more sunlight.<ref name="CSWE" /> A native [[Unidentified Pashvi avian|predatory avian]] [[Species/Legends|species]] that was considered to be dangerous also lived atop the pillars.<ref name="OF" />

==History==
{{Quote|I've been there a few times&mdash;there's a small but stable market for their art, mostly in the Corporate Sector.|Dubrak Qennto|<ref name="OF" />}}
The [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Dubrak Qennto]] had visited Pashvi, the [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Pashvi (species)|Pashvi]] species, on several occasions<ref name="OF" /> by the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[27 BBY/Legends|27 BBY]]<ref name="TERC">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''</ref> in connection to the [[Merchant/Legends|trade]] of Pashvi artworks in the [[Corporate Sector/Legends|Corporate Sector]],<ref name="OF" /> a part of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]].<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> By that year, the Pashvi had fallen prey to a [[Vagaari raids|raid]] by the sentient [[Vagaari/Legends|Vagaari]].<ref name="OF" />

==Inhabitants==
{{Quote|The artist is humanoid. Proportioned differently from humans and Chiss, with either a wider torso or longer arms. There's something of a distance to his emotional state, too. I would say his people are both drawn to and yet repulsed by or fearful of the physical objects they live among.|[[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Mitth'raw'nuruodo]]|<ref name="OF" />}}
Pashvi was home to the sentient Pashvi, a non-violent [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] species that had different proportions than those of the [[Human/Legends|Human]] and [[Chiss/Legends|Chiss]] species.<ref name="OF" /> The [[Plant/Legends|plants]] that grew on the planet's rock spires had one of the highest [[Diet/Legends|nutritional]] values to the Pashvi, and this attracted the native sentients to the pillars. However, the threat posed by the predatory [[Bird/Legends|avians]] simultaneously made the Pashvi afraid of the [[Foodstuff/Legends|edible]] plants and the pillars. These feelings led to a distanced emotional state among the Pashvi themselves and other things they valued.<ref name="CSWE" /> The Pashvi created various works of art, including an elaborate [[Color/Legends|blue]]-and-white [[Unidentified Pashvi sculpture|sculpt]] that had fallen into the hands of Vagaari raiders<ref name="OF" /> by 27 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|BBY]].<ref name="TERC" /> There was a small but stable market for Pashvi art, which was mostly based in the Corporate Sector.<ref name="OF" />

==Behind the scenes==
Pashvi was first mentioned, albeit indirectly, in the [[2006]] novel [[Outbound Flight (novel)|''Outbound Flight'']], written by [[Timothy Zahn]].<ref name="OF" /> The [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' placed the Pashvi [[Star system/Legends|system]], and therefore the planet, in grid square I-5.<ref name="TEA" /> [[Jason Fry]], co-author of ''The Essential Atlas'', has [[:File:JasonFryAtlas.png|stated]] that the star systems listed in the book's Appendix section are named after the most prominent planets or celestial bodies located in those systems. This article therefore considers the homeworld of the Pashvi species to be named in accordance with the Pashvi system.<ref name="Planetnamia" />
